correctness.rationale: The flip energy divided by two is the local spin times its field. Flipping all spins in row two conjugates negative K to q=|K| and preserves both markings. For q=0 a nonconstant row has a wall-adjacent spin with nonpositive flip cost, so only the four pairs of constant rows remain. For q>0 each spin of any unsatisfied rung must agree with both its horizontal neighbors. The unsatisfied rung therefore forces adjacent rungs of the same orientation, and propagation gives only the two opposite constant rows, strict iff q<2J. All other strict configurations have aligned rungs. Their common binary word is unconstrained when q>2J and has no singleton run when 0<q≤2J: a singleton flip is neutral at equality and is not counted. Counting nonconstant cyclic words with k even marked runs of length at least two gives 2n/k times the number of compositions, binomial(n−k−1,k−1); unrestricted even wall sets give 2 binomial(n,k). The wall-marked matrix has trace S_n(z) and characteristic polynomial (t²−t)²−z². Its primitive Perron root is (1+√(1+4z))/2 for z>0, with subleading roots −φ⁻¹ and exp(±iπ/3) at z=1. Exponential moments at z=e^t give limiting per-rung log mgfs by subtracting their t=0 values; the positive spectral gap and differentiability yield concentration at their slopes (5−√5)/10 and 1/2. There are no walls at q=0. The strict threshold and the exact polynomials were separately checked in 36 small-size/coupling cases by comparing total Hamiltonians after every flip. The opening 'two discontinuities' describes the size-growing landscape: the exact all-n theorem has no count increase out of q=0 for the n=3 exception (4 versus 4). The 0<q<2J, q=2J and above-threshold polynomials distinguish the isolated count drop of two at equality.
residual_risks: All-n claims are for the displayed exact polynomials, not the shorthand finite-count jump statement at n=3. Results are strict local minima and uniform counting measures, not laws of states reached under a quench or an equilibrium phase transition.

evidence: Shukla describes parallel rungs and no length-one longitudinal domains on the uniform-coupling ladder. The indexed ANNNI chain's weak stability for 0<κ<1 gives exactly the same cyclic binary words, and its count φ^n+(−φ⁻¹)^n+2cos(nπ/3) agrees with S_n(1) on that record's sizes n≥5.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Every singleton in the ANNNI condition has negative flip cost since its nearest term is −2 and the second-neighbor term is at most 2κ<2. For words with no singletons the first-neighbor term is +2 inside a run or zero at a boundary; at a boundary at least one second neighbor is in the opposing run, so the second-neighbor term is nonnegative. This proves equivalence of the word family and hence of its wall marking, not of the two Hamiltonians or the other ladder sectors.

value.rationale: The simplest periodic ladder with separately variable rung and leg bonds gives a natural comparison of strict trapping landscapes. A local field zero at q=0 or 2J changes the allowed domain structure, and only the exact all-state classification explains both the exponential complexity jumps and the isolated loss of the antiparallel sectors at equality. This is useful as a deterministic benchmark for blocked-state counting and distinguishes entropic proliferation from equilibrium phase behavior; the already-known intermediate word family is not in itself a new contribution.
residual_risks: The interpretation is restricted to strict stability and uniform counting. No claims are made about actual accessibility under dynamics, neutral blocked states, or wider ladders.
